entries.en: Nice to meet you, I'm...
Introduce yourself, say how you are and where you are from, order based on hunger or thirst, and give your number.
Good afternoon and welcome to Café La Esquina! I'm Lupita. How are you?
Hi, I'm Lupita. How are you today?
I'm very well, thank you. And you?
I am well, thank you. (with ser)
I'm from Florida.
Could you repeat that more slowly, please?
Great! I'm very well, thanks. What is your name and where are you from?
What is your name? Where are you from?
My name is Alex. I'm from Gainesville, Florida.
My name is Alex. I am from Gainesville. (with estar)
I'm sleepy.
Could you repeat that more slowly, please?
Nice to meet you, Alex! Are you hungry or thirsty?
Do you want to eat or drink something?
I'm very thirsty. A hibiscus water, please.
I am thirst. A hibiscus water, please.
I'm twenty years old.
Could you repeat that more slowly, please?
Sure. And something to eat? The sweet bread is very good today.
Do you want a sweet bread? It's very good.
Yes, a sweet bread, please. How much is it in total?
Yes, a sweet bread, please. (wrong article)
I'm cold. Where is the restroom?
Could you repeat that more slowly, please?
That's fifty-five pesos. Would you like to earn points? I need your phone number.
That's fifty-five pesos. Can you give me your phone number?
Yes, of course. It's thirty-five, twenty-one, eighty-four, seventy, ninety-six.
Yes, of course. My number is thirty-five, twenty-one, eighty-four... (with estar)
It's fifty-five years.
Could you repeat that more slowly, please?
Perfect! I'll bring your hibiscus water and sweet bread right away. Nice to meet you, Alex!
A table of students
Greet as a group, say where you are from and what you study, and ask questions with qué and cuál.
Hi, guys! How's it going? How are you all today?
Hi. How are you all?
We are very well, thanks. And you, Lupita?
They are fine, thanks.
We are from Texas.
Could you repeat that more slowly, please?
Great! Hey, you all aren't from here, right? Where are you from?
Where are you all from? You're not from here, right?
No, we're not from here. We're from Florida. We're students at the University of Florida.
No, we are from Florida. (with estar)
Yes, we are tired.
Could you repeat that more slowly, please?
How cool! And what do you study?
What do you all study?
I study biology and my friend studies journalism.
We study (I-form) biology and journalism.
We study at eight in the morning.
Could you repeat that more slowly, please?
And which is the hardest class this semester?
Which class is the hardest?
Chemistry. It's very hard! The exam is tomorrow.
Chemistry. They are very hard! (plural verb)
My major is biology.
Could you repeat that more slowly, please?
Hang in there! A little coffee will help you. What would you like to drink?
What are you going to drink?
Which is the most popular coffee?
What is the most popular coffee?
See you tomorrow, Lupita!
Could you repeat that more slowly, please?
The café de olla, with cinnamon! Shall I bring you two?
The café de olla is the most popular. Two?
Yes, two cafés de olla, please. It's really good, right?
Yes, two coffee de olla, please.
I don't know. And you?
Could you repeat that more slowly, please?
My pleasure! That's eighty pesos. Good luck on the exam!
What are you going to do on Saturday?
Ask and tell the time, talk about obligations with tener que and plans with ir a.
Good morning! How can I help you?
Good morning. What do you need?
Good morning. What time does the café close today?
Good morning. What time does the café close? (missing 'a')
It's a quarter past ten.
Could you repeat that more slowly, please?
Today we close at nine at night. Hey, what time is it? My phone has no battery.
We close at nine. What time is it, please?
It's a quarter past ten.
It is (singular) a quarter past ten.
It's Monday.
Could you repeat that more slowly, please?
Thanks! And what can I get you?
What would you like to drink?
An americano, please. I have to study all afternoon.
An americano, please. I have study all afternoon.
I go to the gym every day.
Could you repeat that more slowly, please?
Oh, what a shame! Hey, do you have plans on Saturday? There's live music here at eight.
On Saturday there's music here at eight. Do you have plans?
I don't have plans. What a good idea! I'm going to come with some friends.
Good idea! I'm going come with some friends.
In the summer.
Could you repeat that more slowly, please?
Great! And what are you all going to do after the concert?
What are you going to do afterwards?
We're going to dance and then we're going to have dinner.
We're going dance and have dinner.
We go at a quarter past ten.
Could you repeat that more slowly, please?
Perfect! Here's your americano. That's thirty-five pesos. See you Saturday at eight sharp!
Is there Wi-Fi?
Use hay, ser and estar for places, talk about your classes with -ar verbs, and say what you like.
Good afternoon! Table for one? Are you going to study here?
Do you want a table? Are you going to study?
Yes, thanks. Is there Wi-Fi here?
Yes, thanks. Is Wi-Fi here? (with estar)
Yes, the library is a new building.
Could you repeat that more slowly, please?
Yes, there's Wi-Fi. The password is on the menu. Do you need anything else?
Yes, there is Wi-Fi. The password is on the menu.
Yes. Where is the library? Is it far from here?
Yes. Where is there the library?
Yes. I need to buy a book at the library.
Could you repeat that more slowly, please?
The library is very close, next to the student center. It's a new, very big building. What do you study?
It's close. What do you study?
I study business administration. I'm taking four classes this semester.
I study business administration. He/She takes four classes this semester.
There are four classes in the library.
Could you repeat that more slowly, please?
Nice! And do you like coffee? What can I get you?
Do you like coffee? What would you like?
Yes, I really like coffee. A café de olla, please.
Yes, I really like (plural) coffee. A café de olla, please.
There are many notebooks on my desk.
Could you repeat that more slowly, please?
And something to eat? The cactus tacos are very good.
Do you want to eat something?
No, thanks. I don't like cactus. Just the coffee.
No, thanks. I don't like (singular) cactus.
Yes, where is the gym?
Could you repeat that more slowly, please?
Very good. It's forty pesos for your café de olla. Good luck with your homework!
Do you know the owner?
Use -er/-ir verbs, tell saber from conocer, and describe a person you admire.
Hi! Do you already know what you're going to order?
Do you know what you want?
I don't know yet. I'm not familiar with the menu. What do you recommend?
I'm not acquainted with what to order yet.
Yes, I know Lupita.
Could you repeat that more slowly, please?
I recommend the café de olla. Do you drink coffee every day?
Do you drink coffee every day?
Yes, I drink coffee every morning. A café de olla, please.
Yes, he/she drinks coffee every morning. A café de olla, please.
Yes, I write a letter to my mom.
Could you repeat that more slowly, please?
Same as me! Hey, do you know doña Carmen, the café's owner?
Do you know the owner? Her name is doña Carmen.
No, I don't know doña Carmen. What is she like?
No, I don't know (saber) doña Carmen. What is she like?
Yes, I know how to speak Spanish.
Could you repeat that more slowly, please?
She's very kind and patient, and she always helps everyone. I admire her a lot! And you? Who do you admire?
Doña Carmen is very kind. Who do you admire?
I admire my grandmother. She's brave and understanding, and she always shares everything. She lives with us.
I admire my grandmother. She's brave and understanding. (missing personal a)
I admire the café de olla.
Could you repeat that more slowly, please?
How lovely! This month we vote for employee of the month. Do you know who deserves the award?
Who deserves the employee of the month award?
You, Lupita! You're very nice and hard-working.
You, Lupita! You're very nice and hard-working (masculine).
I don't know. The menu is boring.
Could you repeat that more slowly, please?
Oh, how kind! Thank you so much. Here's your café de olla: that's forty pesos.
A table for the family
Talk about your family with possessives, describe what they look like, and order with stem-changing verbs.
Good afternoon! Table for one?
Is it a table for one person?
No, for four. My parents and my sister are coming in five minutes.
No, for four. My (singular) parents and my sister are coming soon.
Yes, I have a twin sister.
Could you repeat that more slowly, please?
Perfect! What does your sister look like? That way I'll recognize her at the door.
What does your sister look like?
She's tall and thin, and she has curly hair. She looks like my mom.
She's tall and thin (masculine), and she has curly hair.
My sister prefers tea.
Could you repeat that more slowly, please?
Very good. Would you like to order your family's drinks while they arrive?
What would your family like to drink?
Yes. My sister prefers hibiscus water and my parents want two americanos.
Yes. My sister prefers hibiscus water and my parents want two americanos. (no stem change)
Yes. My sister is twenty years old.
Could you repeat that more slowly, please?
I'll serve them right away. And you? What would you like?
What would you like to drink?
I want a café de olla, please. Can I order a sweet bread too?
I want a café de olla, please. Can I order a sweet bread too? (no stem change)
My grandfather is very tall.
Could you repeat that more slowly, please?
Of course! Hey, is that them? The couple at the door?
Are those your parents? The couple at the door?
Yes, those are my parents! And the tall girl is my sister.
Yes, those are your/her parents!
My aunt is divorced.
Could you repeat that more slowly, please?
Welcome! Come in, your table is ready. I'll bring everything right away. It's one hundred sixty-five pesos, but you pay at the end.
Who are you?
Introduce yourself to a classmate, say where you're from, how you are and what you're like.
Hi! Sit down, sit down. I'm waiting for my friend Valeria, but she's always late. My name is Mateo. And you, what's your name?
Hi, I'm Mateo. What's your name?
My name is Alex. Nice to meet you, Mateo.
I am (estar) Alex. Nice to meet you.
I'm fine, thanks.
Could you repeat that more slowly, please?
Likewise. I'm from Sevilla, in Spain. I'm here on an exchange program. Are you from here?
I'm from Spain. Are you from here?
No, I'm not from here. I'm from Florida, in the United States.
No, I'm not from here. I'm from Florida. (with estar)
I'm twenty years old.
Could you repeat that more slowly, please?
Cool! Hey, how are you today? I'm a bit nervous: tomorrow I have my first exam.
I'm nervous about my exam. And you, how are you?
I'm fine, but I'm very sleepy.
I'm fine, but I am (estar) very sleepy.
It's a very pretty café.
Could you repeat that more slowly, please?
I'm sleepy too! Hey, and what are you like? I'm a bit shy, but very adventurous. And your friends? What are they like?
I'm shy. What are you like?
I'm very smart, ha ha! My friends are a lot of fun.
I'm very smart, ha ha! My friends are a lot of fun (singular).
I'm here in the café.
Could you repeat that more slowly, please?
Ha ha! Hey, can you give me your number? That way we can meet up another day with Valeria.
What's your phone number?
Sure. My number is forty-two, fifteen, seventy-eight, thirty, sixty-one.
Sure. My number is (estar) forty-two, fifteen, seventy-eight...
I'm forty-two years old.
Could you repeat that more slowly, please?
Perfect! Oh, look, here comes Valeria! Finally! Great to meet you. See you later!
What do you study?
Greet, talk about your classes and professors, and ask questions with ¿verdad? and cuál.
Hi again! How's it going? How are you?
Hi. How are you?
Hi, Mateo! Very well, and you? You're waiting for Valeria again, right?
Hi, Mateo! We are fine, and you? You're waiting for Valeria again, right?
Bye, Mateo! See you tomorrow!
Could you repeat that more slowly, please?
Yes, late again! Valeria and I are in the same program. We're classmates. You study here, right?
You study here, right?
Yes, I study here. My major is psychology.
Yes, I am (estar) a student here. My major is psychology.
I don't know. What time is it?
Could you repeat that more slowly, please?
How interesting! We study Spanish and communication. What classes do you have this semester?
What classes do you have?
I have biology, history and math. And you all? Which is your favorite class?
I have biology, history and math. What (qué) is your favorite class?
I'm twenty years old.
Could you repeat that more slowly, please?
Literature class! It's hard, but the professors are very good. What are your professors like?
What are your professors like?
My professors are very nice, but the exams are hard.
My professors are (estar) very nice, but the exams are hard.
My professors are at the university.
Could you repeat that more slowly, please?
Valeria and I are very tired this week. And you and your friends? Are you all tired too?
Are you all tired too?
Yes, we're very tired. We have lots of exams!
Yes, we are (ser) very tired. We have lots of exams!
Yes, we're from Texas.
Could you repeat that more slowly, please?
Hang in there! Oh, finally, there's Valeria! Valeria, over here! Well, see you soon!
What are you going to do on Saturday?
Tell the time, talk about plans with ir a and obligations with tener que, and accept an invitation.
Hi! What time is it? Valeria says she's arriving at a quarter past one.
What time is it, please?
It's one thirty.
They are (plural) one thirty.
It's Tuesday.
Could you repeat that more slowly, please?
Oh, she's always late! Hey, what are you going to do this weekend?
What are you going to do on Saturday and Sunday?
On Saturday afternoon I'm going to go to the movies, but on Sunday I have to study.
On Saturday afternoon I'm going go to the movies, but on Sunday I have to study.
My birthday is in March.
Could you repeat that more slowly, please?
Great! We're going to a concert on Saturday at nine at night. Do you want to come with us?
Are you coming to the concert on Saturday at nine?
Yes, of course! What time does it end?
Yes, of course! What time does it end? (missing 'a')
It's nine at night.
Could you repeat that more slowly, please?
It ends at eleven thirty. Afterwards we're going to have tacos for dinner. Do you have plans Sunday morning?
What are you going to do Sunday morning?
Yes, I have to wash my clothes and clean the house. How boring!
Yes, I have to I-wash my clothes and clean the house.
It's in winter.
Could you repeat that more slowly, please?
Ugh, me too! Well, how about we meet here on Saturday at eight thirty?
Shall we meet here on Saturday at eight thirty?
Perfect! See you here on Saturday at eight thirty.
Perfect! See you here on Saturday at eight half (medio).
I have to work on Wednesday.
Could you repeat that more slowly, please?
Great! Look, here comes Valeria... at a quarter to two! Half an hour late, as always. See you Saturday!
Where is the gym?
Help Mateo with campus places using hay, ser and estar, talk about your routine and what you like.
Hi! Hey, can you help me? I still don't know the campus well. Is there a library near here?
Is there a library around here?
Yes, there's a very big library. It's next to the student center.
Yes, a very big library is (estar) next to the student center.
Yes, the bookstore sells textbooks.
Could you repeat that more slowly, please?
Thanks! And where is the gym? I really like to exercise.
Where is the gym?
The gym is far, near the dorm.
The gym is (ser) far, near the dorm.
There's a gym.
Could you repeat that more slowly, please?
Perfect. Hey, do you work or just study?
Do you work or just study?
I study and I also work at the library on Tuesdays and Thursdays.
I study and he/she also works at the library on Tuesdays and Thursdays.
I like the library.
Could you repeat that more slowly, please?
Nice! I take four subjects and spend a lot of time here at the café. Do you like this café?
Do you like this café?
Yes, I like it a lot. It's a very quiet place.
Yes, I like it a lot. It is (estar) a very quiet place.
Yes, there's a café.
Could you repeat that more slowly, please?
Me too. Well, and what don't you like about campus?
What things don't you like about campus?
I don't like dirty, messy classrooms.
I don't like (singular) dirty, messy classrooms.
I like the cafeteria.
Could you repeat that more slowly, please?
Ha ha, you're right! Oh, look, there's Valeria. Thanks for everything! See you on campus!
Do you know Valeria?
Tell saber from conocer, use -er/-ir verbs and describe personal qualities.
Hi! Today you're finally going to meet Valeria... if she arrives. Do you know a lot of people at the university?
Do you know many people here?
Yes, I know many classmates, but I don't know Valeria.
Yes, I know (saber) many classmates, but I don't know Valeria.
Yes, I know how to speak Spanish.
Could you repeat that more slowly, please?
Valeria is very nice and creative. She writes poems, paints and always shares her food.
Valeria is nice and creative. She writes poems.
How nice! And where does Valeria live?
How nice! And where do I-live Valeria?
I write a letter.
Could you repeat that more slowly, please?
She lives in a dorm near campus. We eat together on Fridays. Hey, do you know how to cook?
Do you know how to cook?
Yes, I know how to cook a little. I eat at home almost every day.
Yes, I know (conocer) how to cook a little. I eat at home almost every day.
Yes, I know the restaurant.
Could you repeat that more slowly, please?
Nice! I don't know how to cook at all. Valeria says I'm hopeless, ha ha! And you? What are your best qualities?
What are you like? What qualities do you have?
I'm patient, responsible and very cheerful.
I am (estar) patient, responsible and very cheerful.
I'm from Florida.
Could you repeat that more slowly, please?
So you're like Valeria! Well... she isn't very punctual. Do you think she's coming today?
Do you think Valeria is coming today?
Yes, I think she's arriving soon. I don't know when, but she's coming!
Yes, you think she's arriving soon. I don't know when, but she's coming!
Yes, I eat sweet bread.
Could you repeat that more slowly, please?
Ha ha! Look, there she is! Valeria, come here, I want you to meet someone very special!
My family in Mexico
Talk about families with possessives, describe people and use stem-changing verbs.
Hi! Look, this is a photo of my host family here in Mexico. Do you want to see it?
Do you want to see the photo of my host family?
Sure, I want to see the photo! Who are they?
Sure, I want to see the photo! Who are they? (no stem change)
Yes, I'm twenty years old.
Could you repeat that more slowly, please?
She's my host mother, Carmen, and he's her husband, Jorge. These are their kids, Ana and Luis. And your family? What's it like?
What's your family like?
My family is small. I have a sister and my parents are divorced.
My family is small. I have a sister and my (singular) parents are divorced.
His/your family is very nice.
Could you repeat that more slowly, please?
Oh, and what's your sister like? Do you look alike?
What's your sister like? Do you look alike?
She's tall and dark-haired, and she has long hair. We don't look much alike.
She's tall and dark-haired (masculine), and she has long hair. We don't look much alike.
My sister prefers coffee.
Could you repeat that more slowly, please?
How interesting! Hey, my host family is having a family lunch on Sunday. Can you come?
Can you come to the lunch on Sunday?
Yes, I can! What do they prefer to eat: tacos or enchiladas?
Yes, I can! What do they prefer to eat: tacos or enchiladas? (no stem change)
My cousin plays soccer.
Could you repeat that more slowly, please?
They prefer tacos, of course! Hey, and do you dream of visiting Spain someday?
Do you dream of going to Spain?
Yes! I dream of visiting Sevilla and meeting your family.
Yes! I dream of visiting Sevilla and meeting your family. (no stem change)
Yes, my grandparents are from Texas.
Could you repeat that more slowly, please?
Of course! Oh, look, here comes Valeria with Luis, my host brother. Valeria, Luis, over here! See you Sunday!
